newsitem.title: NORWAY: Offshore loadings started at Statfjord, Gullfaks.
newsitem.headline: Offshore loadings started at Statfjord, Gullfaks.

text.p: Offshore oil loadings resumed early on Monday at North Sea platforms Statfjord and Gullfaks, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said.
"We are loading at both Statfjord and Gullfaks since shortly after midnight (2300 GMT) and production is in full swing," Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said.
North Sea loadings by shuttle tankers have been disrupted recently because of high seas, with the 475,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gullfaks reducing production because of limited storage capacity.
The 360,000 bpd Statfjord maintained full output at the weekend but loadings on Monday were crucial in order to keep up production.

"We expect to be able to continue loading until midnight (2300 GMT) tonight, but it should be enough to maintain full production for some time. The weather is expected to get worse again tomorrow," Steihaug said.
The disruptions at Gullfaks stopped production on Friday at the 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) Tordis field, which is tied back to Gullfaks C.
Tordis, which is operated by Saga Petroleum ASA, was back at normal production on Monday after starting up again on Sunday night, a company spokesman said.
He said Saga's 30,000 bpd Vigdis field resumed production on Sunday night after a gas compressor was repaired. The faulty compressor shut in production last Thursday.
